To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the word-sized visualization that shows all participants and conditions in one plot, the “All-in-one-plot”, is the most suitable for the analysis of eye movement data.

(1) the word-sized visualization that shows the average fixation duration of a word is the most suitable for the analysis of a single participant, (2) the word-sized visualizations that show the number of fixations on a word are the most suitable for a comparison of participants, and (3) the word-sizedvisualizations thatshowthefrequencydistributionoffixationdurationsonawordarethe most suitable for acomparisonofexperimentconditions.

(1) the visualization of the mean eye movement pattern is most useful for analyzing the overall eye movement pattern, (2) the visualization of eye movement patterns of individual participants is most useful for detecting outliers, and (3) the visualization of individual eye movement patterns in relation to the average eye movement pattern is best for analyzing the differences between participants.
